messages:
Maya (Support): Hey team -- Acme App reporting sudden 429s and cost spike this morning when calling rwd3-large with streaming enabled. They say it started after switching to a long-concat streaming flow. Root error: HTTP 429 -> \"rate_limit_exceeded\". They attached a sample request id: req_0b3f8c.

Acme App (Customer): Hi -- we only changed how we stream large payloads (concat chunks to keep latency low). We saw a lot of retries and then an invoice bump. We can share request ids. 429s started at ~08:12 PT.

Maya (Support): Thanks. We looked at headers from a failing call: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rpm-limit: 120
x-rw-rpm-remaining: 0
x-rw-concurrency-limit: 20
x-rw-concurrency-inflight: 21
x-rw-context-tokens: 51200
x-rw-request-id: req_0b3f8c
```

Maya (Support): Noting x-rw-context-tokens ~51200 (they're sending ~50k-token contexts), inflight exceeded concurrency limit by 1. Also customer observed auth latency spikes (ms -> several hundred ms) which caused client to retry.

Ethan (Eng-runtime): I'm pulling serving traces for req_0b3f8c. Early hypothesis: streaming connections are long-lived and hold a slot in concurrency accounting until the whole stream finishes. If clients chunk aggressively while keeping open sockets, concurrency can spike even if per-chunk throughput is low.

Priya (SRE): Correlating at infra level: around 08:10 we saw a short auth-db latency blip (~250ms) across the auth cluster -> caused client SDK to start exponential backoff/retries. That combined with long-lived streams would magnify concurrency.

Lina (CSE): Acme says they retried on 5xx and 429 with immediate backoff (no jitter). So retries were back-to-back. They also upgraded to rwd3-large from rwd2-mid the same day.

Sam (Billing): On the invoice side, retries count toward billed tokens/requests. If they retried payloads and succeeded, tokens billed multiple times. We can provide a line-item breakdown if needed.

Ethan (Eng-runtime): Repro recommendation: simulate many clients that open streaming connections with large context and immediate retry on any non-200. Example curl (streaming simulated):

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-large","stream":true,"input":"'$(python -c 'print("A"*40000)')'"}'
```

Ethan (Eng-runtime): Also try toggling stream on/off to see difference in inflight counts. Instrument: request_id header and /metrics traces.

Priya (SRE): Short-term mitigation we can offer: 1) rate-limit-client-side (recommended), 2) enable client jitter/backoff, 3) suggest switching to non-streaming for very large contexts, or 4) request a temporary concurrency bump for dedicated customers.

Maya (Support): Acme wants a quick workaround + root cause. They've asked whether model context-length affects throttling. Quick answer: yes — longer context increases kernel time and resource reservation per connection which counts against concurrency buckets.

Lina (CSE): I'll propose immediate guidance to Acme: add jitter, cap concurrent streams per host to ~10, and fall back to chunked non-streaming for >32k. Will also offer a short call to walk through SDK best practices.

Sam (Billing): I'll flag potential overbilling and prepare a credit estimate if we confirm retries caused duplicated token charges. Please capture request ids and time ranges.

Ethan (Eng-runtime): Follow-ups for infra/eng: 1) check if concurrency accounting releases on early client disconnects (possible bug), 2) inspect whether streaming sessions block preemption/queue slots, 3) correlate model kernel time with inflight windows. I see a few similar spikes from another customer last month — pattern matches long-lived streaming + auth jitter.

Priya (SRE): We should also consider adding a short-lived burst queue for streaming handoff to avoid hard 429s when auth flaps briefly. But that's product-ey. Filing an ops ticket.

Maya (Support): Acme provided two request ids: req_0b3f8c and req_b7a1d22. They gave a timeline: 08:10 auth slow, 08:12 first 429s, 08:14 retries flooded, 08:20 issue subsided.

Ethan (Eng-runtime): I pulled trace for req_b7a1d22 — shows inflight peaked at 24 for that tenant and keepalive held until final chunk ack. Putting notes into the support ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy rwd3-large-hotfix v2.3.1 completed to canary (hash: 9f8a7c).

Maya (Support): Next actions:
- Lina to send mitigation steps and invite Acme to call.
- Sam to produce provisional billing credit calc.
- Ethan/Priya to investigate concurrency accounting + confirm whether early disconnects free slots.
- Support to ask Acme for exact SDK versions and retry logic.

Acme App (Customer): Thanks — we'll add jitter and reduce concurrent streams to 8 for now. Please let us know if you want test traffic.

Maya (Support): Closing loop once we have infra findings and billing calc. Keeping thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
